C1.rationale: Nearly every hard constraint is load-bearing and states its consequence — the suffix callout, the remote gate, the merge-preservation rule, and the diff-before-write gate all name the failure they prevent, so the model can generalise beyond the enumerated cases; it falls short of 5 only because a few directives (granular Bash patterns, the fixed 'Always include' plugin set, the alphabetised-map instruction) are bare prescriptions with no stated why.

evidence.quote: Wrong suffix in `enabledPlugins` → entry silently ignored (marketplace key does not match). Wrong suffix in the workflow `plugins:` block → action rejects the run.
workflows that cannot run (no remote → no GitHub Actions) should not be scaffolded by default
Use granular patterns only — do not add `Bash(bash *)` for CLI tools.

C2.rationale: The interface is self-describing: every flag is enumerated at the point of declaration in `argument-hint`, each has a `## Parameters` row stating its default, and the Step 4 gate table exhaustively names all six (has_remote × flag) combinations so no interaction is left ambiguous; short of 5 because the bare no-argument invocation and the `--check-only` + `--fix` combination are never defined.

evidence.quote: | `--workflows` | Force-scaffold the `claude.yml` / `claude-code-review.yml` workflows even when no git remote is detected (default: scaffold only when a remote exists). |

C3.rationale: One ~24,000-char file carries everything with no supporting files at all: the rare `--exhaustive` path (~70 lines of derivation tables, composition rules and a sample map), two complete workflow YAML bodies, the full settings stanza, and the report template are inlined alongside the core procedure. It is above a 1 only because the marketplace plugin list is deferred to a runtime query rather than enumerated in the body.

C4.rationale: The unit maintains the same guidance in two places internally: `## Parameters` and `## Flags` are two full tables covering the identical six flags with near-verbatim descriptions, and the two-suffix rule appears in the Step 3 callout, as inline comments in both workflow blocks, and again in Important Notes. Externally, `configure-plugin/skills/configure-repo/SKILL.md` restates the web-session rationale ("extraKnownMarketplaces in .claude/settings.json is the key to surviving ephemeral web sessions") rather than pointing here. The Important Notes bullet does at least cite the canonical table before restating it.

evidence.quote: | `--check-only` | Report current status without making changes |
| `--exhaustive` | Enumerate every marketplace plugin as an explicit `true`/`false` so the project fully overrides global toggles.
`extraKnownMarketplaces` in `.claude/settings.json` is the key to surviving ephemeral web sessions

C5.rationale: This is a skill body, loaded only when the skill fires, not an always-loaded surface like CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules/*.md.

C6.rationale: The genuinely mechanical work — composing the exhaustive enabledPlugins map, merging into an existing settings.json without duplicating entries, deriving each plugin boolean from repo signals, and grouping the diff — is specified in prose for the model to re-derive each run, with no bundled script, schema, or validator. It clears a 1 because the two artifacts it writes are given as exact copy-ready YAML/JSON templates and the marketplace read is a concrete runnable jq/gh command rather than a description.

evidence.quote: Build the full `enabledPlugins` map by reading every plugin name from the two relevant marketplaces, then writing each one with an explicit `true`/`false`.
Render compact (a small markdown table or a `+`/`-` list).

top_finding: Split the file: move the `--exhaustive` derivation/composition path and the two full workflow YAML templates into separately-loadable supporting files (and turn the settings.json merge + map composition into a runnable script), leaving a lean entry point that carries only the default path.
counter_finding: The Step 3 suffix callout table earns its tokens outright — two visually-similar suffix forms whose confusion fails silently in one direction and hard in the other is exactly the non-inferable gotcha a skill should spend tokens on.

leakage.note: Three files on the hard-constraint no-read list (skill-quality.md, skill-development.md, skill-evaluation.md) were auto-injected into my context by the repo's system-reminder mechanism before I saw the task; I did not open them. Notably skill-quality.md names this exact file as its worked size example and mandates the When-to-Use / Agentic Optimizations tables and the REFERENCE.md filename — all on the rubric's exclusion list. I deliberately gave no credit or penalty for the presence of those two tables, and C3 is scored on the absence of any multi-file split (the post's 'divide it into many files'), not on any char threshold or on the REFERENCE.md name. C4's cross-surface finding was discovered independently via Grep over configure-plugin and health-plugin, not from any rule file. Residual anchoring risk on C3 cannot be fully ruled out, but no excluded criterion is cited in any rationale.
